existingReportSummary.executiveSummaryMd: `MedicationKnowledge` is absent from R6 core, so R4 instances are not R6-core valid as the same resource. Top migration concerns are resource-type removal, split mapping across several R6 resources, and loss or remodeling of knowledge-specific sections. The largest uncertainty is the absence of an official migration map explaining intended successors.
existingReportSummary.migrationThemesMd: Migration should start by classifying each R4 `MedicationKnowledge` instance: product identity and basic medication properties may map partly to `Medication` and product-definition resources; ingredient details may map to `Medication.ingredient` or `Ingredient`; contraindications/indications may map to `ClinicalUseDefinition`; regulatory authorization details may map to `RegulatedAuthorization`; packaging may map to `Medication.packageSize` or `PackagedProductDefinition`. Several R4 sections, especially cost, monitoring programs, administration guidelines, and kinetics, do not have an obvious one-resource R6 destination in the reviewed core definitions.
existingReportSummary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high that the same artifact is removed: the named R6 StructureDefinition path is absent, `.index.json` has no `MedicationKnowledge` entry, and package search found no matching artifact. Confidence is medium for the intended replacement analysis because it is inferred from nearby R6 resource structures rather than an official diff, narrative migration page, or ConceptMap.

compatibilityLeverage.note: Resource-level leverage is a planning signal. It does not mark individual Revisit findings as justified or unimportant.

rationaleMd:
MedicationKnowledge has a resource-identity break: MedicationKnowledge StructureDefinition is absent from R6 core. That makes a resource-level migration program unavoidable before element-level compatibility can solve much.

R4 maturity context is trial-use/FMM 0, which creates weak stability pressure.

The computed migration-unavoidability score is 93/100, producing migration shape `removed-or-replaced-resource`, major migration `Yes`, and compatibility posture `migration-program-dominates`.

3 finding(s) identify a yes/partial less-breaking base-design alternative, so the aggregate should not be used to dismiss local avoidability review.

11 shared Resource/DomainResource behavior finding(s) are listed as context but not scored for this resource to avoid duplicating base behavior issues across all resources.
recommendedStandardsPostureMd: Prioritize an explicit migration map, successor-resource guidance, endpoint/search transition guidance, and compatibility profiles or aliases where they are cheap. Do not rely on preserving individual old element names to solve the main break.
